note: D-SINK-18. The verdict vocabulary of the helper's `config shield` verb and the decision table of Model.configShieldDecision, in ONE file because the two sides are joined by a STRING and nothing else would check the join (CLAUDE.md rule 13). tests/test_config_shield.py asserts `verdicts` against the helper's CONFIG_SHIELD_VERDICTS / CONFIG_SHIELD_PRIVATE_VERDICTS and drives the real verb; tests/Model.test.js runs `verdicts` through Model.configShieldState and `decisions` through Model.configShieldDecision and Model.persistCarriesSecret. Rename a verdict on one side only and both suites go red.

verdicts.why: the file denies group and other, either already or because the verb just made it so
a regular file we own whose group/other bits could not be cleared

there is no file at that path. NOT an exposure: no file means no credential in it and nothing to tighten. Collapsing it into `exposed` refused every save, for ever, on a machine that simply had no user config yet -- found by the review
a directory, FIFO or device node sits at that path
the final component is a symbolic link, refused at open by O_NOFOLLOW
the file is owned by another uid, so it is not ours to tighten
something renamed a different file over the path while it was being secured
the open failed for any other reason

unknownVerdictNote: A verdict string neither side knows: a future helper version's answer reaching an older Model.js. It must read as NOT private, which is what makes configShieldState fail closed instead of fail open.

decisions.name: known private, credential in the path
known exposed, credential in the path
no answer yet, EPG URL only
a state string from nowhere is still no answer
clearing the active source is never gated, exposed
clearing the active source is never gated, no answer yet
clearing the active source is never gated, private

decisionsNote: The `secret` column is Model.persistCarriesSecret of the same two URLs, asserted alongside the decision: a row where persistCarriesSecret and the decision disagree would be a gate that is open for a write it believes carries a credential.
verdictsNote: `state` is what Model.configShieldState answers. THREE states, not two: a file that is not there is its own answer. Everything else that is not an unambiguous private fails CLOSED to `exposed`, because each of those means we could not establish that the file is private.
